Every run read SKILL.md first (#1) and ex_unit.md before its first edit. Thinking blocks are redacted in all five transcripts.

Rules changed since the standard (2026-10-22-c at 3e3581d), per git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/: testing.md renamed ex_unit.md with a wider trigger row; a new Formatting bullet under "How to use this skill"; Before you finish step 1; reworded "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" and "Use `do:` for a one-expression body..."; Assert with patterns' == sentence reworded with a new example. Of the case's seven rules only Before you finish changed: step 1 now reads "Run `mix format path/to/file.ex` on any changed file you have not formatted since its last edit (see "Formatting" under "How to use this skill")", and that sentence decides step 1. Following check-10 to check-13, a passing `mix format --check-formatted` on a file after its last edit counts as that file being formatted for step 1, and a `mix test` that compiled the app with no warnings counts as the compile step. The Formatting bullet is not a graded heading; its timing is graded as the case's check line on per-file formatting. The other six rules are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-22-c standard (a total that raises KeyError on an unpriced SKU is clean under the return-tuple rule when its @doc says so; a one-step with is a violation and a case for a single fallible call is not exercised; Map.put/3 on the inner items map inside %{cart | items: ...} is not the pattern the struct rule forbids).

Per-file formatting check line ("`mix format path`, or its `--check-formatted` form, runs on each file before the session edits another file or runs the tests ..."): met in 1 of 5 (opus-1), against 0 of 4 in each of check-10 to check-13, which had no opus run; every Haiku and Sonnet run again wrote lib/shop/cart.ex and then left it for the test file before any format or check. Now the tests."); Edit test/shop/cart_test.exs (#7, #8); a refused `mix format --check-formatted test/shop/cart_test.exs; echo fmt=$?; ...` (#9, refused for the shell variable); `mix format --check-formatted test/shop/cart_test.exs && echo formatted; mix compile --warnings-as-errors ...; mix credo --strict ...; mix test ...` (#10, "formatted", ahead of the compile, Credo and tests). Each file was checked on its own path when it was left and before the tests. haiku-1: Write lib/shop/cart.ex (#8); Write test/shop/cart_test.exs (#9); `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && git diff --no-index /dev/null /dev/null; mix format --check-formatted lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && echo FORMAT_OK; mix deps.get ...; mix compile --warnings-as-errors ...; mix test ...` (#10; FORMAT_OK, one test failed because the rewrite dropped total_quantity/1); Edit lib/shop/cart.ex (#11, restoring total_quantity/1); `mix format --check-formatted lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && echo FORMAT_OK; mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors ...; mix test ...; mix credo --strict ...` (#12, FORMAT_OK). Missed: cart.ex was left for the test Write before its first format, though on its second leaving (#11) it was checked before the tests; the session said "I'm checking formatting on each file first, as the skill asks" while formatting both files in one command. haiku-2: Write lib/shop/cart.ex (#7); Write test/shop/cart_test.exs (#8); Edit test file (#9); a refused chain (#10) `sed -i ... && grep ... && mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && mix format --check-formatted ... && echo FORMAT_OK && git diff --no-index /dev/null /dev/null; mix test ...`; Edit test file with replace_all (#11); `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && mix format --check-formatted lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && echo FORMAT_OK` (#12, FORMAT_OK); `mix test` (#13). Missed for cart.ex (left for the test Write at #8 with no format); the test file was edited three times in a row and formatted when left, before the tests. sonnet-1: a refused python3 heredoc (#4) that would have rewritten cart.ex; Write lib/shop/cart.ex (#5); Write test/shop/cart_test.exs (#6); a refused chain (#7) `cp lib/shop/cart.ex /tmp/before.ex; mix format && diff /tmp/before.ex lib/shop/cart.ex; mix compile ...; mix test ...; mix credo --strict ...`; a project-wide `mix format --check-formatted` with no path (#8, no output, passed); `mix test` (#9); `mix credo --strict` (#10). Missed: never per file and never `mix format` itself; cart.ex was left for the test file before the one check. sonnet-2: a refused python3 heredoc (#6); Write lib/shop/cart.ex (#7); Write test/shop/cart_test.exs (#8); `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && mix test 2>&1 | tail -15` (#9). What the formatter changed or would have changed, by replaying every successful Write and Edit onto the case's files (evals/cases/shop-project) and running `mix format` on each snapshot at the place of each format call; with the formatter's changes applied where the run ran `mix format`, the replayed files are byte-identical to each run's final files in all five runs. opus-1: nothing at #6 (cart.ex) or #10 (test file); there was no wrap to respond to. The `git diff --no-index /dev/null /dev/null` it chains compares nothing; its `sed -n 40,55p lib/shop/cart.ex` printed the remove_item/3 region, whose one-line case clause at line 47 is 97 characters and stayed on one line. haiku-1: nothing at #10 or #12; its `git diff --no-index /dev/null /dev/null` compares nothing, and there was nothing to read. haiku-2: cart.ex unchanged; in the test file the formatter re-indented the `|>` lines under the three `assert {:ok, cart} =` matches (lines 101-102, 110-111 and 119-120, from 8 to 15 spaces), because Edit #11 had put `assert` in front of `{:ok, cart} =` and re-indented only the `Cart.new()` line below it. The harness showed the session the reformatted lines 93-128 as a changed-on-disk snippet, and the session wrote "The "changed on disk" note is just my own `mix format` run." and moved on: it accepted the change, which is the formatter's own indentation of a pipeline after `=` (no `do:` wrap, no literal spread over lines). sonnet-1: the check at #8 passed, so the formatter would change nothing; its refused #7 had planned to diff cart.ex before and after `mix format`. sonnet-2: the format at #9 wrapped cart.ex's `    subtotal = Enum.sum_by(cart.items, fn {sku, quantity} -> Map.fetch!(prices, sku) * quantity end)` after `=` into `    subtotal =` / `      Enum.sum_by(cart.items, fn {sku, quantity} -> Map.fetch!(prices, sku) * quantity end)` (final lines 75-76); the test file was unchanged. The harness showed the session lines 67-84 with the wrap; the session said nothing about it and finished. A wrap after `=` is the formatter's own and stays under the bullet. No run met a `do:` body moved onto its own line or a literal argument spread over several lines, so the bullet's rewrite half was not exercised and no run rewrote a line in response to the formatter.

Before you finish, what each session ran (1 of 5 violated: sonnet-2, step 3). opus-1: after its last edit (#8), #10 ran the check on the test file (passed; cart.ex had been checked at #6 with no later edit), `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (no warnings), `mix credo --strict` (no issues) and a full `mix test` last (19 passed). haiku-1: after its last edit (#11), #12 ran the check on both files (FORMAT_OK), `mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors` (no warnings), a full `mix test` (15 passed) and `mix credo --strict` (no issues). haiku-2: after its last edit (#11), `mix format` and the check on both files (#12), a full `mix test` (#13, `==> shop / Compiling 1 file (.ex) / Generated shop app`, 15 passed), `mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors` (#14, no warnings) and `mix credo --strict` (#15, no issues). sonnet-1: after its last edit (#6), a project-wide `mix format --check-formatted` (#8, passed), a full `mix test` (#9, `==> shop / Compiling 1 file (.ex) / Generated shop app` with no warnings, 19 passed) and `mix credo --strict` (#10, no issues); no separate mix compile and never mix format itself, both counted per the judgement calls. sonnet-2: after its last edit (#8), only `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && mix test 2>&1 | tail -15` (#9; the app compiled with no warnings, 16 passed); it never ran Credo, and its reply says so: "I didn't run `mix credo --strict`, which the skill asks for when a project has Credo." Step 3 decides that verdict. In every run the last `mix test` was the full suite with no edit after it.

Chain fallible steps with `with`: opus-1 writes a two-step with in apply_discount/2 (lines 74-77: parse_discount/1 then ensure_no_discount/1, each a private function, no else), clean. sonnet-1 writes two one-step with blocks (apply_code/2 lines 74-76 on parse_code/1, total/2 lines 100-102 on subtotal/2), the rule's first "Instead of", so violated; it rejects a second code in a function head (line 79). The Haiku runs and sonnet-2 write no with and handle each single fallible call with case (haiku-1 lines 65-68, haiku-2 lines 60-63, sonnet-2 lines 56-59), not exercised. Against 2026-10-22-c (0 of 5 violated, all not exercised), sonnet is back to violated, as in 2026-10-22-b.

Other rules, graded to the 2026-10-22-c standard. Atoms: opus-1 (lines 108-110), haiku-2 (91-93), sonnet-1 (113-115) and sonnet-2 (89-91) use one parse clause per code string; haiku-1 trims and upcases, then maps with explicit case clauses (lines 85-88). defstruct: opus-1 and haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 `[:items, :discount]`, haiku-2 `[:items, :discount_code]`, all bare atoms. Return tuples: tagged-tuple or atom reasons everywhere. An unpriced SKU raises KeyError in four runs: haiku-1 (doc lines 75-76) and haiku-2 (doc line 80) say it raises; opus-1 (doc lines 92-93) and sonnet-2 (doc lines 69-70) say `prices` "must hold every SKU in the cart", a stated precondition that makes a missing price the caller's bug, which this grade counts as the @doc saying so (judgement call; their replies also explain the KeyError). sonnet-1 returns {:error, {:unknown_sku, sku}}. Money: integer div in all five (opus-1 line 119 rounding the discount down, haiku-1 line 97 and haiku-2 line 99 rounding halves up, sonnet-1 line 125 `div(subtotal * 90 + 50, 100)`, sonnet-2 line 93 rounding the discount down). Naming: domain names throughout, no boolean, get, fetch, size or length functions. Not graded but checked: no break of the reworded do: rule (sonnet-1's block at lines 79-81 and sonnet-2's at lines 62-64 are one-expression clauses whose do: form would be 123 and 103 characters, which the formatter would move, so a block is what the rule asks for) or of the multi-line-argument rule (no call takes a multi-line literal; sonnet-2's test head at lines 77-80 spreads its context pattern over lines, a pattern, not a call argument). other_violations: opus-1 single-step pipes in two doctests (lib lines 36 and 97) and haiku-1 a two-step pipe on one line inside a case head (line 85), both under the pipeline rule as in earlier grades; haiku-2 two bind-then-== test pairs (test lines 60-61 and 65-68) under Assert with patterns. The original test file's pipelines starting with `Cart.new()` are the project's convention and are not listed.

BOGUS returns {:error, {:unknown_discount, "BOGUS"}} in opus-1 and {:error, {:unknown_code, "BOGUS"}} in the other four. An unpriced SKU raises KeyError except in sonnet-1, which returns {:error, {:unknown_sku, "KIWI"}}. No lib file has String.to_atom/1 or a float.
